That is, the nominal rate of interest should equal zero and the optimal tax on money should be zero. The critical property of money, according to Correia and Teles, is its status as a free primary good. Free in this context means that it can be produced at zero variable cost. The costless production assumption is standard in monetary economics, and it provided the intuition for Friedman’s original result. With a zero social cost of production, optimality requires that the private cost also be zero. This occurs only if the nominal rate of interest is zero.
